waivers.reason: Reached only through the Metro bundler and Expo CLI at build time, on archives this repo produces itself. The shipped app contains no tar parser and never handles an untrusted archive. Advisory: node-tar: Decompression/parse DoS via unlimited input
Used for build-time identifiers. The size argument is never attacker-controlled -- every call site passes a literal. Advisory: nanoid: custom generators can loop indefinitely when size is zero

Build-time only, via Metro. No shell command in this app is constructed from user input; the shipped bundle spawns no process at all. Advisory: shell-quote: Quadratic-complexity Denial of Service in `parse()` (CWE-407)

Transitive through Expo asset processing at build time, on images committed to this repository. The app decodes no untrusted image dimensions. Advisory: image-size: JXL and HEIF parsers allow denial of service through infinite loops

Reached only at build time through the Expo CLI (expo -> @expo/cli -> node-forge, and again via @expo/code-signing-certificates), which uses it to sign expo-updates manifests. This app declares no updates or codeSigning block in app.config.ts and never imports expo-updates, so it neither produces nor verifies a signature, and the shipped bundle contains no RSA verifier. No patched release exists at any version -- npm's only offered fix is a semver-major expo bump, which would change the SDK. Advisory: node-forge RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements

Reached only through the Metro bundler and Expo CLI at build time, on archives this repo produces itself. The shipped app contains no tar parser and never handles an untrusted archive. Advisory: node-tar: Negative tar entry size causes infinite loop in archive replace
Reached only by the Metro dev server websocket during development. Production builds contain no websocket client or server. Advisory: ws: Memory exhaustion DoS from tiny fragments and data chunks

Reached only at build time through Metro's file map (expo -> @expo/metro -> metro-file-map -> micromatch -> braces), which expands glob patterns this repository writes itself in its Metro and Jest configuration. No pattern is attacker-controlled, and the shipped bundle contains no glob expander. No patched release exists at any version -- npm's only offered fix is a semver-major @jest/transform bump. Advisory: braces vulnerable to stack-exhaustion denial of service through deeply nested patterns
